ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a transformer, and beside the secondary winding is marked “10V”; the two ends of the secondary are connected to the single-phase bridge rectifier circuit composed of four diodes on the right side; the output terminal of the bridge rectifier is connected to the load on the right side. Reasoning: The question asks for the maximum reverse voltage of diode D in the bridge rectifier circuit. By convention, the 10V in the figure is the RMS value of the transformer secondary AC voltage. In a single-phase bridge rectifier, in each half-cycle a pair of diodes conducts, and the maximum reverse voltage borne by the non-conducting reverse-biased diode is equal to the peak value of the transformer secondary voltage, not twice the peak value. Therefore the maximum reverse voltage PIV(D) = Vm = sqrt(2) × 10V = 14.14V.

raw_record.question_text: In the single-phase bridge rectifier circuit shown in the figure, what is the maximum reverse voltage of diode D?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: note the transformer secondary labeled 10V connected to a four-diode bridge rectifier and a load on the right. Then read the question as asking for the maximum reverse voltage of a bridge diode D. Treat the 10V label as the RMS value of the AC secondary. In a bridge rectifier, when one pair of diodes conducts, a reverse-biased diode sees at most the instantaneous secondary peak voltage. Therefore PIV(D) = Vm = sqrt(2) * 10V = 14.14V.
